title: A uniform principal localization lifts coordinate idempotents
statement: Let A and B be commutative rings with B an A-algebra. Let K be a field with an A-algebra structure, K' a field with compatible K- and A-algebra structures, r a natural number, and L_j fields with K'-algebra structures for j in Fin(r). Fix a K'-algebra equivalence e from the quotient of (K tensor_A B) tensor_K K' by its nilradical onto the product of the L_j. Here the nilradical is the ideal of nilpotent elements. Assume K is a fraction field of A. Let R0 be a domain with compatible maps A to R0 to K' making K' a fraction field of R0. There exists nonzero t in R0 such that, for every s divisible by t and every principal localization R=R0[1/s] in the universe of A, with compatible maps A to R0 to R to K' and K' a fraction field of R, and every compatible R-algebra structure on the L_j, every compatible R-algebra homomorphism f from (B tensor_A R) modulo its nilradical to the product of the L_j contains each coordinate vector: for every j there exists x in its source such that f(x)_i is 1 for i=j and 0 otherwise. Call f compatible when for every b in B its value on the class of b tensor 1 is e of the class of (1 tensor b) tensor 1. No finiteness or Noetherian hypothesis is required.

proof.text: Put C = (B tensor_A R0)_red. Tensor associativity and localization of the nilradical identify its generic localization with the given product via e. For each of the finitely many coordinate idempotents, choose a numerator in C and a nonzero R0 denominator. Take t to be the product of these denominators. It is nonzero because R0 is a domain. If t divides s, every denominator divides s, hence is a unit in R0[1/s]. Map the chosen numerator to (B tensor_A R)_red and multiply it by the inverse of the image of its denominator. Its image in the generic product is exactly the desired coordinate idempotent. Compatibility on pure tensors, together with R-linearity and surjectivity of the quotient, identifies any specified f with this canonical map, so the construction works for every such f. For r = 0 choose t = 1; there is no coordinate to lift. Neither injectivity nor Noetherianity is used.

    (A : Type u) [CommRing A]

    [IsFractionRing R0 K']
    (r : ℕ) (L : Fin r → Type (max u v)) [∀ j, Field (L j)]
    [∀ j, Algebra K' (L j)]
    (e :
      letI := Algebra.TensorProduct.rightAlgebra (R := K) (A := K ⊗[A] B) (B := K')
      (((K ⊗[A] B) ⊗[K] K') ⧸
        nilradical ((K ⊗[A] B) ⊗[K] K')) ≃ₐ[K'] (∀ j, L j))
    : ∃ t : R0, t ≠ 0 ∧ ∀ s : R0, t ∣ s →
      ∀ (R : Type u) [CommRing R] [Algebra R0 R] [IsLocalization.Away s R]
        [Algebra A R] [IsScalarTower A R0 R] [Algebra R K']
        [IsScalarTower R0 R K'] [IsFractionRing R K']
        [∀ j, Algebra R (L j)] [∀ j, IsScalarTower R K' (L j)],
        letI := Algebra.TensorProduct.rightAlgebra (R := A) (A := B) (B := R)
        ∀ f : ((B ⊗[A] R) ⧸ nilradical (B ⊗[A] R)) →ₐ[R] (∀ j, L j),
            (∀ b : B, f (Ideal.Quotient.mk _ (b ⊗ₜ[A] (1 : R))) =
              e (Ideal.Quotient.mk _ (((1 : K) ⊗ₜ[A] b) ⊗ₜ[K] (1 : K')))) →
          (∀ j, ∃ x, ∀ i, f x i = if i = j then 1 else 0)
